title: The best video editing software in 2026
summary: We tested all the top video editors, and this is the video editing software that came out on top—including free video editors, mid-range options, and professional video editing software.
body_markdown:
**Best for**


**Standout feature**


**Pricing**


Adobe Premiere


A professional suite of video editing tools


Everything you could possibly need in a video editor


$22.99/month


DaVinci Resolve


A free, cross-platform option


Cut or Edit: two different workflows for editing


Generous free option available; $295 for Studio edition


Final Cut Pro


Apple users who want a pro-level editor


Unbeatable performance on Apple hardware


$299.99 or $12.99/month as part of the Apple Creator Studio subscription


Clipchamp


Web-based edits from anywhere


Convenient web-based editing plus a ton of integrations and other features


Free plan available; Microsoft 365 subscription required for $9.99/month to remove watermark and export above 1080p


Adobe Premiere Elements


Enthusiasts looking to balance features and price


Three different editing modes for quick, guided, and advanced video editing


Free trial available; $149.99 for 3 years


Kapwing Video Editor


Editing full projects in your browser


Browser-based editing that feels responsive and fast like desktop software


$16/month per editor


Flixier


Video editors who want generative AI tools at their fingertips


Access to a broad range of image, video, and audio generative models


$19/month for 1080p exports and 2,000 credits to spend; $39/month for 4K exports and 10,000 credits


Kdenlive


A free, open-source option


A straightforward video editor for all desktop users


Free on Widows, Mac, and Linux
